I saved the results to `/work/answer.json`. I checked the numbers by hand against the intermediate totals (by segment, category and month).

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Top Q3 segment by net sales | enterprise, 331,539,488 KRW |
| b. Customers with a paid Q3 order | 249 |
| c. Top Q3 category by net sales | acc, 234,478,195 KRW |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-08 |
| e. Customer with the largest Q3 refunds | u41@ex.com (2,979,950 KRW) |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid Q3 orders | 232 |
| g. Average net sales per paid Q3 order | 702,344 KRW |
| h. Change from August to September | -14.9% (net sales fell) |

**One judgment call that affects answer a:** I counted customers by email, which turns 300 accounts into 250 people. But some of those people have accounts in different segments; for example, u110@ex.com has one smb account and one enterprise account. For segment totals I used the segment of the account that placed each order, not one segment per person. If you want each person tied to a single segment, the answer to a could change.

Other things I checked:
- Some segment values had stray spaces or capital letters (" consumer", "Enterprise ", "SMB"). After cleaning they group into three segments: consumer, smb and enterprise.
- There is no duplicate refund row for the same order and product. Every refund matches an order line, and no refund quantity is larger than the quantity ordered.
- All timestamps are stored as UTC. I added 9 hours to each one before deciding its date and month.

STATUS: DONE
